QTREX Quantum to Unveil 17,280-Line Cryogenic Interconnect Architecture at IEEE Quantum Week 2026

Cryogenic interconnect developer QTREX Quantum Ltd. (Nasdaq: QTEX) has announced plans to publicly unveil an ultra-high-density interconnect architecture capable of supporting up to 17,280 coaxial lines per cryogenic stage inside commercial dilution refrigerators . The architecture will be demonstrated physically at IEEE Quantum Week 2026 (Booth 712) in Toronto, Canada, from September 13–18, 2026.

Monolithic AME Manufacturing vs. Discrete Coaxial Assemblies

Conventional cryogenic interconnects rely on networks of discrete coaxial cables, individual connectors, and manual stage-by-stage thermal anchoring assemblies that suffer from volumetric congestion, thermal load limits, and assembly variability as qubit counts scale . QTREX’s architecture distributes transmission lines across both the perimeter and plate area of each cryogenic stage:

Monolithic Integration: Manufactured using Additively Manufactured Electronics (AME) technology acquired earlier in 2026 , the interconnect structures combine signal conductors, dielectric layers, crosstalk shielding, and mechanical routing into a single engineered assembly .

Thermal and Spatial Optimization: Designed to replace discrete cable wiring harnesses, reducing component interfaces and thermal dissipation bottlenecks inside the cryostat .

Capacity Milestone: The capacity of over 17,000 lines per stage represents more than double the density of any previously disclosed physical interconnect architecture for commercial dilution refrigerators.

Structured Configuration Programs and Customer Pipeline

Following the Toronto presentation, QTREX will launch structured configuration programs to convert customer technical requirements—spanning quantum processor types, cryostat geometry, channel mixes, and thermal budgets—into tailored engineering configurations and commercial proposals.

Led by CEO Dagi Ben Noon, QTREX is shaping initial manufacturing specifications around engagements with commercial quantum computing vendors, U.S. federal laboratories, defense organizations, and university research centers .
